top.title: Late INT by Thomas Georgeadis preserves Class AA semifinal win for Saratoga Springs football
top.description: Saratoga Springs quarterback Bobby Morris looks for a receiver during the Section 2 Class AA semifinals against Shaker on Friday in Saratoga Springs. (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - During an evening that featured 871 yards of offense and 77 points, defense ultimately won out for the Saratoga Springs football team. Shaker found itself deep in Blue Streaks' territory during the final minute of Friday's thrilling Section 2 Class AA semifinal showdown ,trailing by seven points. But, Saratoga junior linebacker Thomas Georgeadis put an end to Shaker's comeback aspirations when he intercepted a pass to help preserve a wild 42-35 victory over the Blue Bison. These two teams met in Week 5 at Saratoga Springs and the Blue Streaks easily prevailed 42-20 in a game that was not remotely as close as the final score would indicate. Friday night, Shaker fell behind twice by 21 points and refused to go away in a game where the Blue Bison outgained Saratoga Springs by 145 yards. "That was a great game by Shaker. They definitely did a good job. The came with a good game plan and their kids were very physical," Saratoga Springs coach Eric Hayden said. "Hats off to them. We found a way to win and that is all that matters." "I am so happy for the team," Saratoga Springs senior quarterback Bobby Morris said. "We graduated a lot of guys from last year's team (that beat CBA 14-13 for the title), but the new guys we have stepped up into new roles and done a hell of a job. I am really proud of them for that. We've got a big opponent next week coming off a big win. This wasn't the Super Bowl. We are happy, but we're not satisfied." The victory by Saratoga Springs (9-1 overall), winners of the 2025 sectional title, sends them back to the Super Bowl for a rematch against top-seeded Christian Brothers Academy (10-0) Nov. 14 at Colonie High School. Saratoga Springs led 28-14 at halftime and expanded the lead to 35-14 in the third quarter. "A lot of times this season, our offense has not performed to its potential," Morris said. "Defensively, they've had our backs. This game, I don't think the defense played to their standard, but the offense had their backs. That is the thing with this team: we all have each other's backs. It is something special and something dangerous, especially in the playoffs." Saratoga fans cheer for their team during the Section 2 Class AA semifinals against Shaker on Friday in Saratoga Springs. (Jim Franco/Times Union) Key moment On a night where defense took a back seat to offensive efficiency, Georgeadis helped secure the Super Bowl berth with his interception. "That kid deserved that play by far," Morris said. "That kid is the definition of football in my head. I watch his film all the time. His life is football, football, football. What a play." Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Usman Khawaja’s new book makes a startling claim about the 2018 Cape Town scandal, popularly known as the "Sandpapergate." top.title: Saint Louis fights off Mizzou to win Show Me Showdown
top.description: Saint Louis burst onto the scene last year with a 24-1 start to the season and an NCAA Tournament victory. Josh Schertz, the man behind the special 2024 Indiana State team, put together one of the most fun teams in the country last season and had a handful of returners. Everyone knew getting good opponents on the schedule was a challenge, but on Friday, the Billikens had an opportunity against an in-state rival in Missouri. With possibly their biggest game of the season staring them in the face, Schertz’s group didn’t blink. Saint Louis controlled the Show Me Showdown and beat Mizzou 90-84. Despite the game’s magnitude, Saint Louis was more than ready. “In these games, you got to believe you belong,” Schertz said. “You can’t look at yourself as some sort of ‘lesser than.’” The “Atlantic-10 Splash Bros” set the tone early for Saint Louis. After a 3-0 Mizzou start, Ishan Sharma buried a 3 that resulted in a four-point play. Trey Green hit a 3 before Mizzou head coach Dennis Gates could use his first timeout of the game. By the time Gates got his team over to talk, it was Saint Louis by eight. The hot start for the Billikens continued as they went into the halftime break shooting nearly 57% from the field and 56% from distance. Mizzou forward Bryson Tiller noted how good Saint Louis’ offense is. “With Sharma and Green, those [other] guys, they can really spread the floor,” Tiller said. “Michaeli can really drive it.” Saint Louis didn’t slow down in the second half, but did have to withstand multiple late Mizzou pushes. It was Alon Michaeli who sealed the game with a couple of key baskets and free throws in the final two minutes. “He had played a good game up until the final two minutes… but the scoring down the stretch was huge for us,” Schertz said. Saint Louis held Mizzou five-star freshman Jason Crowe Jr. to just 3-for-18 shooting from the field. Schertz credited Quentin Jones for his defense on Crowe Jr. throughout the game. “Amari (McCottry) and Kellen (Thames) were on the All-Defensive team, and I would make a case that Q is the best individual defender of all those guys,” Schertz said. As the final buzzer sounded, the Billikens and their fans were ecstatic. Over the summer, Trey Green and Ishan Sharma said that they had the Mizzou game circled. On Friday, Saint Louis proved that they were no one-year wonder. Even without Robbie Avila, who was barred from playing for Saint Louis on Friday by the College Sports Commission , Saint Louis was the better team against a high-major team with a ton of talent. “The best way to get what you want in your life is to deserve what you want in your life,” Schertz said.

top.description: EVANSVILLE — Memorial coach John Hurley was asked this week how many sectional championships he has won. He didn't know the number off hand, nor was it important. All of his attention and emphasis was on the next opportunity. Hurley, now in his 19th season at his alma mater, knows not to anticipate anything easy once the calendar turns to November. Just ask his undefeated teams the last two seasons. A singular pointed goal: extend the season another week. More: Southwestern Indiana high school football sectional finals updates, scores No. 1 Memorial defeated No. 8 Mater Dei 28-7 on Friday, Nov. 6 at Reitz Bowl to win the Class 3A sectional championship. Far from a masterpiece performance – too many penalties, for starters. The result was still the same. The Tigers (11-0) stood firm behind its defense in the second half to reach the regional round for the first time since 2023. "You get to this time of the year, anything can happen," Hurley said. "We're just going to keep grinding away at it. I'm just proud of the kids. I know what they've done to get to this point." No offensive explosion or head-turning sequence this week . Memorial was simply the tougher team. The defense limited the opponent to only 174 total yards – a miniscule 2.3 yards per carry when factoring in sacks. The only scoring drive for Mater Dei came in the first quarter after converting a fake punt. The Wildcats only ran around a dozen offensive plays after halftime. The major reasoning: the Tigers won every notable moment on defense. Kellan Carter forced a fumble midway through the third quarter. Rhylan Brogden made a fourth down stop. top.title: Mavericks’ Dusty May gives props to ‘winning player’ Morez Johnson Jr. for big game vs. Jazz
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Mavericks’ Dusty May gives props to ‘winning player’ Morez Johnson Jr. for big game vs. Jazz appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks dominated the struggling Utah Jazz en route to a 112-100 win in the NBA Cup. The game was a memorable one for Morez Johnson Jr., who had a breakout game as he notched the first double-double of his career with 13 points and 17 rebounds, including an impressive 10 offensive boards. Mavericks head coach Dusty May , who also coached Johnson when they were at Michigan, was full of praise for the rookie . May noted that after a slow start in part due to a lower leg injury during preseason, Johnson is getting back to his best physically. “The first glimpse was in San Antonio when Naji (Marshall) threw the lob, and ‘Rez went up and got it. Even though he didn’t finish it, that was the first glimpse when the staff said, ‘Okay, his athleticism is almost back,'” May said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) May also applauded the fact that Johnson can still put up big numbers despite not getting his number called on many plays. “His energy, his effort. He’s a winning player, and for a guy you don’t call any plays for, if you can get him 13 and 17 without calling any plays for him. We need those types of glue guys,” May added. Heading into the game, Johnson was averaging 7.4 points and 3.1 rebounds in eight games, all off the Mavs bench. But as his performance against Utah showed, the No. 9 pick in this year’s draft of capable of a lot more. His game figures to be a nice complement to Cooper Flagg, who has the skillset of a potential top-10 player . As Johnson continues to get back to peak fitness, he figures to provide some much-needed energy and physicality to the Mavs in the frontcourt. Saint Stephen’s 29, St. Edwards 6 The Falcons turned their relentless rushing attack and stingy defense into a 29-6 victory over the Pirates in an SSAA 11-man BOUND bracket quarterfinal game at the Moore Athletic Complex at Turner Fields. The next assignment for the Falcons (8-4) will be a semifinal game at home next Friday against Oxbridge Academy (9-3), whic defeated Glades Day, 22-21, in its quarterfinal game. The Pirates (7-5) jumped out to a 6-0 lead in the first quarter on an 11-yard TD pass from junior Dylan Colontrelle to sophomore Chase Colontrelle before the Falcons scored 29 unanswered points. The Saint Stephen’s defense slammed the door, forcing the Pirates to turn the ball over on downs four times in Saint Stephen’s territory, including three times inside the Falcons 10-yard line. “That was really frustrating,” Pirates head coach Rich Schofield said. “I felt like our defense was out there a ton. That’s a really good football team.” The Falcons also recovered two fumbles to stop potential St. Edwards’ scoring drives. “Our defensive line really came off the ball,” Falcons head coach Chris Valcarcel said. “We went to a 5-man line and we were able to dominate. top.description: ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov went down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6, and the card’s MMA and submission grappling action kept the energy high from beginning to end. A heavyweight grappling trilogy between a pair of World Champions was settled in a flash, ending a rivalry nearly a decade in the making. Plus, two undefeated debutants squared off in a grinding bantamweight clash with a perfect record on the line, while an unbeaten rising star went the distance in a tightly contested atomweight chess match. Finally, a strawweight clash that opened with a grappling scare ended in a choke and could lead to a World Title opportunity. Here’s what happened in the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 49. Lee Sinks In Rear-Naked Choke To Submit Lalthazuala View this post on Instagram “The Flash” Lee Seung Cheol may have just earned a crack at the ONE Strawweight MMA World Title. The South Korean handed Nazareth “The Northstar” Lalthazuala his first career loss, as he submitted the Indian phenom via rear-naked choke in the second round of a match that was filled with plot twists. Most of the opening frame was spent on the canvas, with Lalthazuala hunting for submissions and even getting close to securing a choke. The Indian MMA star looked like he’d be gliding toward an easy win. But Lee weathered the storm, and he returned more determined in the second stanza. The 27-year-old South Korean had his opponent trapped against the ropes and rained down ground-and-pound. Lalthazuala threw up-kicks until he could create enough space to stand, but the two soon went back to the mat and battled for position. Lee won that battle, as he took the back of the 25-year-old and sunk in the choke for the tap at the 3:04 mark of round two. That submission win moved Lee’s record to 14-1, put him on a 14-bout winning streak, and inched him closer to a shot at ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion Joshua Pacio , who will defend his belt at ONE SAMURAI 5 on November 18. top.title: LeBron James avoids 'depths of hell' from Cavs fans, but scoring scarce in loss
top.description: CLEVELAND — Akron native LeBron James still has the date on the tip of his tongue: Dec. 2, 2010. It's when James visited the Cavaliers for the first time as a member of the Miami Heat and experienced the wrath of enraged Cleveland fans who felt betrayed by "The Decision." Nearly 16 years later, James visited the Cavs (5-4) for the first time as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers (8-2) on Friday, Nov. 6, receiving loud cheers during player introductions and a mostly warm reception, albeit mixed with some booing, in the Cavs' 119-95 blowout victory . James said it was "great" how Cavs fans received him in his latest homecoming game. But was the 2003 St. Vincent-St. Mary High School graduate wondering how it would go after he left the Los Angeles Lakers this past summer and announced on July 24 he would sign with the 76ers in free agency instead of his other primary suitors, the Cavs, Heat, Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves? "I don't know because at the end of the day, nothing can get as worse as Dec. 2 2010, from a reception standpoint," James said. "So, I've seen damn near the depths of hell when it comes to reception here all the way to, like, the heavens above. So, anything in between is easy money." In a rare occurrence, scoring did not prove to be easy for the 41-year-old James. He finished with a season-low eight points on 3-of-12 shooting from the field (0 of 4 on 3-pointers), seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers in 32 minutes. "Too many turnovers on my behalf, and I didn't feel in a rhythm offensively all day," James said. "... Every game has its own challenges, and I don't think [we played well] offensively as a group. And I know I damn sure wasn't good at all." Cavs news: How the Cavaliers spoiled LeBron James' most recent Cleveland homecoming game The NBA's all-time leading scorer, James has failed to reach double figures in scoring in just 10 regular-season games in his career. His streak of 396 consecutive regular-season games with double-digit scoring in Cleveland was snapped, according to ESPN. "The biggest thing is just making it tough [on James]," Cavs guard Donovan Mitchell said. "He's a hell of a player, but [we were] just trying to pack the paint and knowing that he's trying to drive to also kick. He had six turnovers, and you give credit where it's due to our defense as a whole. From there we were able to get out and get going." The Cavs avenged their 114-106 season-opening loss on Oct. 22, when Cleveland blew a 29-point lead during James' first home game in Philadelphia. In the rematch, Mitchell scored a game-high 23 points to go along with seven rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Forward Evan Mobley compiled 22 points, six rebounds, four assists, a steal and a blocked shot. top.title: Captain Shreve’s Gabe Lockett dials in dominating runs against Byrd
top.description: Byrd fans looking for a storybook ending to their otherwise disappointing season Friday night against archrival Captain Shreve instead came away licking their wounds at Lee Hedges Stadium. Powered by the undauntable legs of senior Gabe Lockett , the Gators rolled 48-21 in the 49th running of the Backyard Brawl, which annually pits neighbor against neighbor in one of the longest running rivalry games in Northwest Louisiana. Lockett rushed for 336 yards and 5 TDs with four of the scores and 212 of the yards coming in the first half, when the Gators (5-4) dominated the Jackets (1-9). Lockett averaged 14.6 yards per carry while delivering TDs on runs of 11, 4, 63, 38 and 60 yards. “I knew this was an important game because we needed a home game,” Lockett said. “Coming into the game I was dialed in and running hard. They couldn’t stop us. They couldn’t stop the run. Couldn’t stop the pass. I’m proud of my guys and we’re gonna go and do it next week.” MAXIMUM EFFORT: Byrd’s Maxie sets record in loss as Haughton, BTW, Northwood win PREDICTIONS: Top Shreveport-Bossier high football games in Week 10 predictions The game ends the season for Byrd, while the Gators will find out Sunday if they did enough to warrant a home LHSAA playoff game in the first round as expected. Shreve’s victory means the Gator seniors went 4-0 against the Jackets, which is a rarity in the series. The Shreve defense held record-setting Byrd running back Christian Maxie to just 127 yards and one late TD when the game was out of hand. The senior concludes his career with 4,577 yards, the most in school history. “That was our best collective effort defensively,” said Shreve coach Jeremy Wilburn, a former Byrd quarterback. “We were prepared from a scheme standpoint. top.title: 'I'm never going to give up!' - Everton star Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall sends message to Thomas Tuchel with Coventry goal hours after England squad snub for Jobe Bellingham
top.description: FBL-ENG-PR-EVERTON-COVENTRY - AFP Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall vowed to keep fighting for a maiden international call-up after scoring in Friday night's 3-1 Premier League victory over Coventry City. The 28-year-old found the net at Hill Dickinson Stadium just hours after England boss Thomas Tuchel overlooked him in favour of Jobe Bellingham. Midfielder responds on Merseyside pitch Dewsbury-Hall channelled his frustration into an emphatic display on Friday evening as his fierce strike helped Everton secure consecutive top-flight wins and climb to fifth in the table. Tipped to make the cut for this month's Nations League matches following a strong run of form, the playmaker learned earlier that day that Borussia Dortmund teenager Bellingham had been selected ahead of him . Even so, Tuchel acknowledged on Friday afternoon that the Toffees man had been "very close" to inclusion after enjoying "a very good season". Playmaker vows to keep fighting Reflecting on his omission while speaking to Sky Sports after the comeback triumph over Coventry, Dewsbury-Hall said: "It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie. It's a massive dream of mine to play for my country. I know I was close. [I'm] sad, yeah, but really proud of myself and how I have reacted. All I can keep doing is putting in good performances and hopefully one day I get the nod, because I'm never going to give up." Tactical freedom sparks Merseyside revival Overcoming obstacles is nothing new for the midfielder, who had EFL loan spells at Blackpool and Luton Town before making his Premier League bow for boyhood club Leicester City at 22, suffering relegation and winning the Championship under Enzo Maresca. After following the Italian to Chelsea for £30 million and being largely restricted to cup outings during his sole campaign at Stamford Bridge, he joined Everton in summer 2025 and has since recorded 11 league goals and seven assists. Praising his current role on Merseyside, Dewsbury-Hall said: "I'm really, really enjoying it. I've got a really good hybrid role in this team, where the gaffer is giving me the freedom to pop up all over the pitch." Reiterating his international determination, he added: "I've got the mentality. I'll keep pushing and pushing and see what happens." March window offers next opportunity With the November international break now underway, Dewsbury-Hall faces a four-month wait until March for his next chance to earn an England call-up. Maintaining his clinical output across the winter schedule will be essential as he looks to keep Everton in contention for European qualification. Continuing to thrive in his free-roaming midfield role could finally force Tuchel's hand when the Three Lions reconvene in the spring.

top.description: Naugatuck's Qwentarvous Lee had a 68-yard touchdown pass and TD runs of 18 and 29 yards while finishing with 142 yards on 14 carries in a 41-14 win over Seymour on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, at Naugatuck High School. (Roger Cleaveland/Hearst Connecticut Media) NAUGATUCK - Going into this high school football season, there was some uncertainty in Naugatuck as to how good the Greyhounds could be. Although the team had some offensive talent, coach Chris Anderson needed to see something more from his players. He wanted to see them play with heart, with conviction for one another and with an attitude befitting a champion. "Our team motto is, ‘Earn it,'" Anderson said. "Since Day 1, we have told them the only thing we are entitled to is the air we breathe. Everything else we have to go earn. We felt like we lost that a little bit last year. We had a little entitlement and issues like that. We wanted to get back to old-fashioned hard work, and ‘Earn it' has been our rally cry." That rallying cry could be heard loud and clear throughout Craig Peters Field on Friday night as the Greyhounds remained undefeated with a dominant 41-12 win over a very good Seymour team that had won five games in a row. Qwentarvous Lee scored two touchdowns and threw for another. Brandon Andoh rushed for a game-high 145 yards, scored two rushing touchdowns and caught a 68-yard touchdown pass, and the Naugatuck defense held a potent Wildcats offense in check to complete the total team effort. Seymour had scored 44 points or more in each game of its winning streak, but Naugatuck intercepted three passes and forced the Wildcats to turn the ball over on downs three times while the Greyhounds ran out to a 21-0 lead and cruised to their eighth win of the season without a loss. The Naugatuck defense set the tone early, as the Greyhounds stopped Seymour on a 4th-and-9 play at the Naugy 34-yard line on the Wildcats' first possession of the game. Then Naugy needed only five plays to score on a 57-yard pass play from Sean DiBona to Malachi Kinchen. Seymour drove deep into Naugatuck territory on its second possession, but again came away with nothing when Kinchen intercepted Max Brito's pass on fourth-and-8 from the Greyhounds' 18-yard line, creating a major momentum swing. Eric Harriott and MJ Delpino also intercepted passes for the Naugatuck defense, which was led by inside linebacker Josiah Loyd, Raily Hernandez and Isaiah Portalatin. "I can tell you that we have definitely improved on defense from the beginning of the season," Kinchen said. "Our defense looked a little shaky in the beginning of the season, but our coaches made adjustments and put players in spots they needed to be, and they made plays." Quarterback Max Brito led Seymour offensively with 77 yards on 17 carries, while Connor Shea finished with 58 yards on 11 carries. They each scored a touchdown. nigeria.description: Within a span of one week, opposition political parties in Nigeria have experienced various challenges in their bid to contest in the 2027 general elections. From the bids for the presidency to governorship, national assembly and state assembly seats, opposition candidates have not been finding it easy to campaign as they wish as they are faced with various forms of harassment, suppression and intimidation. Weekend Trust reports that 31 states in the country are under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) while two of the remaining five opposition governors have been included in the presidential campaign council of the party. Our correspondents recall that within the week, the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) was attacked in Cross Rivers State, while the bid by the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to hold a rally in Sokoto met with stiff opposition and in Edo and Plateau States, the billboards of major opposition candidates were pulled down. On Thursday, a Federal High Court sitting in Abuja also nullified all the processes of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) that led to the emergence of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgement, nullified the emergence of the former Senate President, David Mark, Rauf Aregbesola and others as national officers of the ADC. According to reports from the campaign team, thugs blocked the convoy and pelted vehicles with stones. These developments, according to political observers, represent a systematic weakening of opposition parties and raise concerns over Nigeria’s democracy. Due to the frequency in occurrence, opposition figures and civil society organisations have accused the ruling party, APC, of utilizing state-backed coercion, judicial manipulation, and targeted inducements to systematically dismantle counter-balancing political structures across the country. In that span of time he held many positions – Assistant Adjutant General, Provost Marshal, Commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy. He also served as the governor of the old Oyo State in 1978. nigeria.title: Trump: Lesson for Nigeria, by Stephanie Shaakaa
nigeria.description: Donald Trump wanted the November 3 midterm elections to be about him. He said so repeatedly, urging Americans to vote as though his name were on the ballot. He wanted a Republican victory to demonstrate that his presidency still commanded popular support and that his influence over American politics remained firmly intact. Well, Americans took him seriously. Perhaps more seriously than he expected. Democrats have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress, delivering a major electoral setback to Trump and his Republican Party. Yet, as the results became clear, Trump reached for an explanation that seemed to contradict his own campaign message. In a post on his Truth Social platform, he declared: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The irony is difficult to miss. He had spent weeks asking Americans to treat the election as a verdict on his presidency. When the verdict went against him, he suddenly appeared to be distancing himself from it. He wanted the political benefits of making the election about him without accepting the consequences when voters delivered an unfavourable answer. For readers in Nigeria, it is worth explaining what America calls midterm elections and why they matter. In the United States, a president is elected for a four-year term, but congressional elections take place every two years. This means that halfway into a president’s tenure, Americans return to the polls to elect members of the legislature. These elections are called midterms because they take place in the middle of a presidential term. Congress has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, while senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the 100 Senate seats contested every two years. Midterm elections do not determine who becomes president. The sitting president remains in office. Instead, voters decide which party controls Congress and, by extension, how much support or opposition the president will face in the legislature This gives Americans an opportunity to express satisfaction or dissatisfaction with a president’s performance without waiting another four years. They can strengthen the president’s party in Congress or hand control to the opposition, making it considerably more difficult for the president to advance his legislative agenda. That is precisely what has happened to Trump. American presidents often benefit from what is known as the coattail effect. When a president is popular, candidates from the same party can benefit from that popularity. His political strength becomes an advantage for others seeking elective office. But when a president becomes unpopular, the effect can work in reverse. Candidates associated with his administration may find themselves paying the price for public dissatisfaction with his leadership. nigeria.title: From open pavilion to nation of orderlies: Is Zik’s ‘fear-free’ Nigeria still possible?
nigeria.description: .What a 1960 inauguration says about fear in today’s corridors of power By Omeiza Ajayi Nearly 66 years after Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was sworn in as Nigeria’s first African Governor-General, the footage of that day – which has again recently gone viral – raises an uncomfortable question: why did a leader who held the highest office in the land need no retinue of security details standing behind him, while today every minister, and even some local government supervisors, cannot move without a swarm of details? The inauguration took place on November 16, 1960, at Tafawa Balewa Square, barely six weeks after independence. It was also Zik’s 56th birthday. The narrator of the newsreel set the scene plainly. “At the steps of the pavilion stand the Prime Minister and the Lord Chief Justice, symbolising the people and the law, on what is surely one of the most important occasions in the history of the country.” No armed escort looms in the frame. No aide hovers at the shoulder of the man the crowd was chanting for. “Zik! Zik!” rang around the square as he arrived, and the vast stands, in the narrator’s words, were “hushed.” Today the picture is reversed. In Abuja and in the state capitals, orderlies trail ministers into halls and offices. The situation is so bad that some security personnel actually enter into very enclosed spaces or rooms with their AK47 rifles in clear breach of security protocol. At the local government level, some unelected supervisory councillors have been known to move with armed vigilance team members or hunters, sometimes to intimidate the very people they were appointed to serve. The easy explanation is insecurity, and it is not a false flag. Banditry, kidnapping and insurgency have made parts of the country dangerous, and no leader can be faulted for fearing for his life. But the leaders of other nations also face threats. Behind the American president or a British prime minister stand trained protective officers, assigned to a defined danger. They do not crowd every public official, from the cabinet room to the ward office, with men whose chief duty is to announce importance. It is not uncommon in Nigeria to see security details standing and blocking a television camera. That leaves the harder question. Are Nigeria’s leaders afraid of the general state of the country, or have they become afraid of their own people? Zik, standing in the open that November morning, appeared to have settled that question for himself. He began his address with these words: “It is with humility, mingled with joy, that I thank this grand concourse of patriots and friends of Nigeria for congregating here today on the occasion of my inauguration as the first African Governor General and Commander-in-Chief of the Federation of Nigeria.” He titled the speech “Respect for Human Dignity,” and he made no secret of what he feared for Nigeria. nigeria.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. nigeria.title: Scientists turn cancer cells into weapons against tumours
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe What if the chemical produced in abundance by cancer cells could be turned against the cancers? What if, instead of flooding the entire body with powerful drugs in an attempt to destroy a tumour, scientists could persuade cancer cells to manufacture destructive chemicals from within? That possibility is at the centre of an intriguing scientific breakthrough in Japan, where researchers have developed an experimental technique that exploits carbon monoxide produced by cancer cells to generate cancer-killing compounds inside them. The approach turns an unusual feature of cancer biology into a potential therapeutic advantage. Rather than administering an already manufactured toxic drug that circulates through the body and can damage healthy tissues, the researchers have devised a chemical system that produces an anticancer compound inside targeted cancer cells. In laboratory experiments, the technique successfully generated toxic compounds in several cancer cell lines while leaving a noncancerous cell line without detectable production of the same compound. Although still at an early experimental stage, the findings could open a new direction in cancer treatment, particularly in the long-standing search for ways to destroy malignant cells while sparing healthy tissues from the collateral damage associated with conventional chemotherapy. The research, led by Katsunori Tanaka at the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), Japan, was published in Nature Communications. Cancer treatment has long been complicated by a fundamental problem: drugs powerful enough to destroy malignant cells can also injure normal cells. Chemotherapy, for instance, often affects healthy tissues because many anticancer medicines cannot distinguish perfectly between cancerous and noncancerous cells. The resulting damage can produce debilitating side effects, including nausea, fatigue, hair loss and suppression of the immune system. Scientists have consequently been exploring more selective ways of delivering or generating anticancer agents at the precise location where they are needed. Tanaka and colleagues focused on carbon monoxide, a gas commonly recognised for its toxicity but also naturally produced in small quantities in the human body. Their strategy was to deliver a metal-based catalyst into cells and use the available carbon monoxide as the chemical fuel for a reaction that manufactures an anticancer substance. In principle, the reaction would be activated predominantly in cancer cells, where sufficient carbon monoxide is available, rather than in healthy tissues. The research represents part of a developing scientific field known as therapeutic in vivo synthetic chemistry, which seeks to use chemical reactions inside living organisms to manufacture therapeutic substances where they are needed. nigeria.title: Nigeria is losing $1.6bn yearly to avoidable blindness — Aghaji
nigeria.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru Almost on a daily basis, across Nigeria and much of Africa, millions of people wake up to a world they cannot see clearly. A farmer peeks at his cassava farms for instance, but cannot differentiate the difference between weed and crop. A trader holds her register at arm’s length, guessing at figures she once read at a glance. A child in the back row of a classroom copies from a board that is almost a blur. More often, an old woman needs her grandchild to lead her to the market because the road she walked for over 50 years has become unrecognizable. Those are not statistics. They are the human face of a crisis that Africa has lived with for too long. As Professor Ada Aghaji told a packed hall at the University of Nigeria on October 29, 2026, this is a crisis Africa can no longer afford to ignore. Delivering the institution’s 254th Inaugural Lecture, titled “Let There Be Sight: Building Sustainable Eye Health Systems for All in Africa,” Aghaji, Professor of Ophthalmology and Eye Health Systems, made a simple but very powerful argument: eye health in Africa is not just a medical issue. It is an economic issue. A development issue. A justice issue. And the numbers prove it. According to her, Nigeria loses an estimated $1.6 billion every year in productivity because of vision impairment. Across Africa, the loss is about $9 billion. Globally, it stands at a staggering $410 billion. Behind those figures are livelihoods cut short, schooling interrupted, and families pushed deeper into poverty. Yet, as Aghaji stressed, much of this vision loss can be prevented or treated. A pair of spectacles costing less than a bag of rice. A 15-minute cataract operation. A routine screening at a primary health centre. Why, then, do millions of Africans continue to live with avoidable blindness when the solutions already exist? That was the question at the heart of her lecture. Two Children, Two Worlds Perhaps the most haunting moment of the lecture came not from statistics, but from a story. Aghaji spoke of two children born with congenital rubella syndrome; a condition that can cause cataracts, deafness and other disabilities. One was born in Nigeria. He received timely surgery, spectacles and hearing aids, and with them, a chance to learn, to play, to grow Their medical conditions were similar. Their opportunities were profoundly different. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. business.title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . business.title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Show And Availability Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Saint Louis fights off Mizzou to win Show Me Showdown
sports.description: Saint Louis burst onto the scene last year with a 24-1 start to the season and an NCAA Tournament victory. Josh Schertz, the man behind the special 2024 Indiana State team, put together one of the most fun teams in the country last season and had a handful of returners. Everyone knew getting good opponents on the schedule was a challenge, but on Friday, the Billikens had an opportunity against an in-state rival in Missouri. With possibly their biggest game of the season staring them in the face, Schertz’s group didn’t blink. Saint Louis controlled the Show Me Showdown and beat Mizzou 90-84. Despite the game’s magnitude, Saint Louis was more than ready. “In these games, you got to believe you belong,” Schertz said. “You can’t look at yourself as some sort of ‘lesser than.’” The “Atlantic-10 Splash Bros” set the tone early for Saint Louis. After a 3-0 Mizzou start, Ishan Sharma buried a 3 that resulted in a four-point play. Trey Green hit a 3 before Mizzou head coach Dennis Gates could use his first timeout of the game. By the time Gates got his team over to talk, it was Saint Louis by eight. The hot start for the Billikens continued as they went into the halftime break shooting nearly 57% from the field and 56% from distance. Mizzou forward Bryson Tiller noted how good Saint Louis’ offense is. “With Sharma and Green, those [other] guys, they can really spread the floor,” Tiller said. “Michaeli can really drive it.” Saint Louis didn’t slow down in the second half, but did have to withstand multiple late Mizzou pushes. It was Alon Michaeli who sealed the game with a couple of key baskets and free throws in the final two minutes. “He had played a good game up until the final two minutes… but the scoring down the stretch was huge for us,” Schertz said. Saint Louis held Mizzou five-star freshman Jason Crowe Jr. to just 3-for-18 shooting from the field. Schertz credited Quentin Jones for his defense on Crowe Jr. throughout the game. “Amari (McCottry) and Kellen (Thames) were on the All-Defensive team, and I would make a case that Q is the best individual defender of all those guys,” Schertz said. As the final buzzer sounded, the Billikens and their fans were ecstatic. Over the summer, Trey Green and Ishan Sharma said that they had the Mizzou game circled. On Friday, Saint Louis proved that they were no one-year wonder. Even without Robbie Avila, who was barred from playing for Saint Louis on Friday by the College Sports Commission , Saint Louis was the better team against a high-major team with a ton of talent. “The best way to get what you want in your life is to deserve what you want in your life,” Schertz said.

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks dominated the struggling Utah Jazz en route to a 112-100 win in the NBA Cup. The game was a memorable one for Morez Johnson Jr., who had a breakout game as he notched the first double-double of his career with 13 points and 17 rebounds, including an impressive 10 offensive boards. Mavericks head coach Dusty May , who also coached Johnson when they were at Michigan, was full of praise for the rookie . May noted that after a slow start in part due to a lower leg injury during preseason, Johnson is getting back to his best physically. “The first glimpse was in San Antonio when Naji (Marshall) threw the lob, and ‘Rez went up and got it. Even though he didn’t finish it, that was the first glimpse when the staff said, ‘Okay, his athleticism is almost back,'” May said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) May also applauded the fact that Johnson can still put up big numbers despite not getting his number called on many plays. “His energy, his effort. He’s a winning player, and for a guy you don’t call any plays for, if you can get him 13 and 17 without calling any plays for him. We need those types of glue guys,” May added. Heading into the game, Johnson was averaging 7.4 points and 3.1 rebounds in eight games, all off the Mavs bench. But as his performance against Utah showed, the No. 9 pick in this year’s draft of capable of a lot more. His game figures to be a nice complement to Cooper Flagg, who has the skillset of a potential top-10 player . As Johnson continues to get back to peak fitness, he figures to provide some much-needed energy and physicality to the Mavs in the frontcourt. sports.description: ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov went down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6, and the card’s MMA and submission grappling action kept the energy high from beginning to end. A heavyweight grappling trilogy between a pair of World Champions was settled in a flash, ending a rivalry nearly a decade in the making. Plus, two undefeated debutants squared off in a grinding bantamweight clash with a perfect record on the line, while an unbeaten rising star went the distance in a tightly contested atomweight chess match. Finally, a strawweight clash that opened with a grappling scare ended in a choke and could lead to a World Title opportunity. Here’s what happened in the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 49. Lee Sinks In Rear-Naked Choke To Submit Lalthazuala View this post on Instagram “The Flash” Lee Seung Cheol may have just earned a crack at the ONE Strawweight MMA World Title. The South Korean handed Nazareth “The Northstar” Lalthazuala his first career loss, as he submitted the Indian phenom via rear-naked choke in the second round of a match that was filled with plot twists. Most of the opening frame was spent on the canvas, with Lalthazuala hunting for submissions and even getting close to securing a choke. The Indian MMA star looked like he’d be gliding toward an easy win. But Lee weathered the storm, and he returned more determined in the second stanza. The 27-year-old South Korean had his opponent trapped against the ropes and rained down ground-and-pound. Lalthazuala threw up-kicks until he could create enough space to stand, but the two soon went back to the mat and battled for position. Lee won that battle, as he took the back of the 25-year-old and sunk in the choke for the tap at the 3:04 mark of round two. sports.title: LeBron James avoids 'depths of hell' from Cavs fans, but scoring scarce in loss
sports.description: CLEVELAND — Akron native LeBron James still has the date on the tip of his tongue: Dec. 2, 2010. It's when James visited the Cavaliers for the first time as a member of the Miami Heat and experienced the wrath of enraged Cleveland fans who felt betrayed by "The Decision." Nearly 16 years later, James visited the Cavs (5-4) for the first time as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers (8-2) on Friday, Nov. 6, receiving loud cheers during player introductions and a mostly warm reception, albeit mixed with some booing, in the Cavs' 119-95 blowout victory . James said it was "great" how Cavs fans received him in his latest homecoming game. But was the 2003 St. Vincent-St. Mary High School graduate wondering how it would go after he left the Los Angeles Lakers this past summer and announced on July 24 he would sign with the 76ers in free agency instead of his other primary suitors, the Cavs, Heat, Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves? "I don't know because at the end of the day, nothing can get as worse as Dec. 2 2010, from a reception standpoint," James said. "So, I've seen damn near the depths of hell when it comes to reception here all the way to, like, the heavens above. So, anything in between is easy money." In a rare occurrence, scoring did not prove to be easy for the 41-year-old James. He finished with a season-low eight points on 3-of-12 shooting from the field (0 of 4 on 3-pointers), seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers in 32 minutes. "Too many turnovers on my behalf, and I didn't feel in a rhythm offensively all day," James said. "... Every game has its own challenges, and I don't think [we played well] offensively as a group. And I know I damn sure wasn't good at all." Cavs news: How the Cavaliers spoiled LeBron James' most recent Cleveland homecoming game The NBA's all-time leading scorer, James has failed to reach double figures in scoring in just 10 regular-season games in his career. His streak of 396 consecutive regular-season games with double-digit scoring in Cleveland was snapped, according to ESPN. "The biggest thing is just making it tough [on James]," Cavs guard Donovan Mitchell said. "He's a hell of a player, but [we were] just trying to pack the paint and knowing that he's trying to drive to also kick. He had six turnovers, and you give credit where it's due to our defense as a whole. From there we were able to get out and get going." The Cavs avenged their 114-106 season-opening loss on Oct. 22, when Cleveland blew a 29-point lead during James' first home game in Philadelphia. In the rematch, Mitchell scored a game-high 23 points to go along with seven rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Forward Evan Mobley compiled 22 points, six rebounds, four assists, a steal and a blocked shot. sports.title: Captain Shreve’s Gabe Lockett dials in dominating runs against Byrd
sports.description: Byrd fans looking for a storybook ending to their otherwise disappointing season Friday night against archrival Captain Shreve instead came away licking their wounds at Lee Hedges Stadium. Powered by the undauntable legs of senior Gabe Lockett , the Gators rolled 48-21 in the 49th running of the Backyard Brawl, which annually pits neighbor against neighbor in one of the longest running rivalry games in Northwest Louisiana. Lockett rushed for 336 yards and 5 TDs with four of the scores and 212 of the yards coming in the first half, when the Gators (5-4) dominated the Jackets (1-9). Lockett averaged 14.6 yards per carry while delivering TDs on runs of 11, 4, 63, 38 and 60 yards. “I knew this was an important game because we needed a home game,” Lockett said. “Coming into the game I was dialed in and running hard. They couldn’t stop us. They couldn’t stop the run. Couldn’t stop the pass. I’m proud of my guys and we’re gonna go and do it next week.” MAXIMUM EFFORT: Byrd’s Maxie sets record in loss as Haughton, BTW, Northwood win PREDICTIONS: Top Shreveport-Bossier high football games in Week 10 predictions The game ends the season for Byrd, while the Gators will find out Sunday if they did enough to warrant a home LHSAA playoff game in the first round as expected. Shreve’s victory means the Gator seniors went 4-0 against the Jackets, which is a rarity in the series. The Shreve defense held record-setting Byrd running back Christian Maxie to just 127 yards and one late TD when the game was out of hand. The senior concludes his career with 4,577 yards, the most in school history. “That was our best collective effort defensively,” said Shreve coach Jeremy Wilburn, a former Byrd quarterback. “We were prepared from a scheme standpoint. I thought we had our guys in good positions to make plays and then they made those plays. We came back out at halftime and maintained that aggressive mentality on defense.” Byrd still leads in the series 29-20, but has lost its domination of the Gators. The Jackets had won 26 of the last 31 meetings with Shreve before the current run. “I think this group of seniors has understood the process a little more each year of how to prepare for a game like this and not let the moment be too big,” Wilburn said. “We had so many guys participate in such a productive way that it was truly a collective effort from all three phases. And we’re super proud of that.” Jimmy Watson covers Louisiana sports for the USA TODAY Network. Email him at jwatson@shreveporttimes.com and follow him on Twitter @JimmyWatson6. sports.title: 'I'm never going to give up!' - Everton star Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall sends message to Thomas Tuchel with Coventry goal hours after England squad snub for Jobe Bellingham
sports.description: FBL-ENG-PR-EVERTON-COVENTRY - AFP Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall vowed to keep fighting for a maiden international call-up after scoring in Friday night's 3-1 Premier League victory over Coventry City. The 28-year-old found the net at Hill Dickinson Stadium just hours after England boss Thomas Tuchel overlooked him in favour of Jobe Bellingham. Midfielder responds on Merseyside pitch Dewsbury-Hall channelled his frustration into an emphatic display on Friday evening as his fierce strike helped Everton secure consecutive top-flight wins and climb to fifth in the table. Tipped to make the cut for this month's Nations League matches following a strong run of form, the playmaker learned earlier that day that Borussia Dortmund teenager Bellingham had been selected ahead of him . Even so, Tuchel acknowledged on Friday afternoon that the Toffees man had been "very close" to inclusion after enjoying "a very good season". Playmaker vows to keep fighting Reflecting on his omission while speaking to Sky Sports after the comeback triumph over Coventry, Dewsbury-Hall said: "It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie. It's a massive dream of mine to play for my country. I know I was close. [I'm] sad, yeah, but really proud of myself and how I have reacted. All I can keep doing is putting in good performances and hopefully one day I get the nod, because I'm never going to give up." Tactical freedom sparks Merseyside revival Overcoming obstacles is nothing new for the midfielder, who had EFL loan spells at Blackpool and Luton Town before making his Premier League bow for boyhood club Leicester City at 22, suffering relegation and winning the Championship under Enzo Maresca. After following the Italian to Chelsea for £30 million and being largely restricted to cup outings during his sole campaign at Stamford Bridge, he joined Everton in summer 2025 and has since recorded 11 league goals and seven assists. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. technology.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
technology.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. technology.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
technology.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says.
